title.en: Janev electron-impact ionization rate for H and H2
title.zh: Janev原子氢与分子氢电子碰撞电离率

summary: Evaluate separate H and H2 Maxwellian electron-impact ionization-rate fits from electron temperature in eV.

capability: Janev electron-impact ionization rate for H and H2
Species-specific Maxwellian electron-impact ionization rate coefficients for H and H2 from electron temperature in eV.
operation: Evaluate the Janev H or H2 electron-impact ionization rate coefficient
electron temperature in eV and target species H or H2 -> ionization rate coefficient in m^3/s
discovery.model: Janev species-specific logarithmic-polynomial Maxwellian rate fits; not a runtime cross-section integral.
discovery.geometry: None; pointwise scalar or array temperature samples with no spatial axis inferred (coordinate: electron temperature in eV).
discovery.boundary: Temperature must be finite and strictly positive; the target species must be exactly H or H2; out-of-range temperatures clip to the fit endpoints and the output must be finite and positive.

identity.relation: H or H2 electron-impact Maxwellian ionization rate coefficient from a species-specific logarithmic polynomial
identity.direction: electron temperature in eV and target species H or H2 -> ionization rate coefficient in m^3/s
identity.definition: Clip strictly positive electron temperature to [0.1, 2.01e4] eV, then evaluate exp(polyval(log(T), a_species))*1e-6 m^3/s with the ascending-power nine-coefficient Janev table for the selected H or H2 branch. Preserve the input shape and NumPy polynomial evaluation order.
identity.model: Janev H and H2 Maxwellian ionization-rate fits; not a runtime cross-section integral
identity.geometry: none; pointwise scalar or array temperature samples
identity.coordinates: electron temperature in eV, with no spatial axis inferred
identity.boundary: finite real numeric temperature strictly positive; target species exactly H or H2; endpoint clipping; finite positive represented output
assumptions: The two coefficient tables, the 1e-6 unit conversion and the polynomial evaluation order define the fit on finite positive real temperatures.
H and H2 are distinct target species; the caller selects a branch explicitly. The rate coefficient alone does not construct a density-scaled source or sink.
This callable rejects zero and negative temperatures and does not coerce boolean or numeric-string inputs; the declared positive real input contract is the only accepted domain.

inputs.name: electron_temperature_ev
inputs.description: Electron temperature for the selected Maxwellian ionization fit.
inputs.constraints: Finite and strictly positive; positive values outside [0.1, 2.01e4] eV are clipped to the nearest endpoint.

inputs.name: target_species
inputs.description: Select the atomic-H or molecular-H2 ionization fit.
inputs.constraints: Exactly H or H2; no fallback branch.

outputs.name: rate_m3_s
outputs.description: Selected electron-impact ionization Maxwellian rate coefficient.
outputs.constraints: Finite and strictly positive on accepted inputs; no external physical accuracy is asserted.

preconditions: The caller supplies electron temperature in eV, chooses H or H2 explicitly, and accepts endpoint clipping.
supported: Scalar and array pointwise evaluation of the H and H2 Janev ionization fits on or clipped to their declared temperature interval.
excluded: Other target species, density-scaled source or sink assembly, collisional-radiative state coupling, and direct velocity-mesh averaging of a cross section.
Physical accuracy claims outside the compared fit or without an external atomic-physics reference.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError for non-real numeric or non-finite temperature, nonpositive temperature, or target species other than the scalar strings H and H2. Boolean, complex and numeric-string temperature coercions are rejected.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises ValueError if the derived rate is non-finite or nonpositive; no partial output is returned.

example.description: Evaluate both target branches and their clipped endpoints.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.collisions import evaluate_janev_electron_impact_ionization_rate
t = np.array([0.01, 10.0, 50000.0])
h = evaluate_janev_electron_impact_ionization_rate(t, 'H')
h2 = evaluate_janev_electron_impact_ionization_rate(t, 'H2')
edge = evaluate_janev_electron_impact_ionization_rate(np.array([0.1, 10.0, 20100.0]), 'H')
assert h.shape == (3,) and np.all(np.isfinite(h)) and np.all(h > 0.0)
assert np.array_equal(h, edge)
assert not np.allclose(h, h2, rtol=1e-12, atol=0.0)
example.expected: Three positive H rates, exactly clipped at both endpoints and numerically distinct from H2 rates.

scope: Fixed reference values verify both species-specific coefficient tables at six temperatures, including both fit endpoints.
Direct tests cover branch distinction, clipping, scalar shape, invalid target species, invalid temperature and non-real coercion rejection.

No external implementation comparison is maintained or replayed by this repository; the maintained tests validate the declared relation against an in-repository independent formulation and cover the stated rejection and clipping behaviour only on their tested grids.
verification.evidence_ceiling: The tests establish the discrete two-branch fit, clipping and failure contract on tested samples. Bit-exact agreement with the in-file independent evaluation of the same expressions holds on the compared grids only. No external atomic-physics oracle validates either fit; public distribution licensing is absent.
known_limitations: No external physical-reference oracle is bound; this gap remains open.
Out-of-fit-range positive temperatures silently repeat endpoint rates rather than extrapolating or failing.
A rate coefficient is not a complete source or sink without caller-supplied density and state contracts.
No environment-gated external-implementation comparison exists in this repository; any earlier external comparison is not replayed by the maintained tests.

The ionization fit has a single maximum in electron temperature, at about 137 eV for H and 156 eV for H2; the peak locations are fit properties, not independently validated thresholds, and the rate is not monotone on either side of them.
